newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli mayor says Jerusalem Arab building cancer.
newsitem.headline: Israeli mayor says Jerusalem Arab building cancer.

text.p: Israel's mayor of Jerusalem said on Monday that building by Arabs without permits was a cancer threatening Israel's hold on the holy city and vowed a relentless demolition drive.
His comments came amid an intense Israeli-Palestinian struggle for control over Arab East Jerusalem sparked by Israel's groundbreaking on a Jewish settlement in March.

Israel's Haaretz newspaper said Palestinians in East Jerusalem had built more than 1,000 structures without permits over the last six months. A city spokeswoman confirmed hundreds of "illegal" houses were being built but did not elaborate.
"The building crimes in East Jerusalem have ceased to be a marginal problem in this or that area," the newspaper quoted mayor Ehud Olmert as saying.
"This is a cancer that directly threatens Israel's sovereignty in Jerusalem and undermines the basic infrastructure of the web of life in the unified city," he said.
"It is my intention to prepare for massive enforcement, including intensive carrying out of demolition orders and I don't plan on compromising any more on anything," Olmert said.
The municipality spokeswoman confirmed the quotes.

Palestinians complain that Israel, eager to tighten its grip on East Jerusalem which it captured from Jordan in the 1967 Middle East war and later annexed, systematically denies Palestinians building permits.

"The Palestinians in East Jerusalem are suffering from a housing shortage for years...The Palestinians simply have no room to expand. It is very difficult to obtain building permits," Ahmed Tibi, an aide to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, said in remarks broadcast by Israel Radio.

"Olmert, to his credit, said clearly and unequivocally that he doesn't want the Arab population in East Jerusalem to grow," he said, referring to recent comments made by Olmert on the population of Jerusalem.
Olmert last week said he was alarmed by figures released by a research institute which showed the Arab population growth rate in Jerusalem was much higher than that of Jews.

The institute said that of 603,000 people living in East and West Jerusalem, 422,300 were Jews and 180,700 were Arabs and others. It said that the average growth rate of Arabs was 4.5 percent compared with 1.3 percent for Jews.
Israel and the PLO have agreed in their 1993 peace deal to negotiate the future of East Jerusalem at the end of a series of interim self-rule accords for Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
In March, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government began building 6,500 housing units for Jews on a West Bank hill that has been annexed to Jerusalem.
